summary: Module 4 BREAK: The IDOR on the invitation endpoint. Symptom given: a non-admin user can invite to a team they don't manage -- POST /teams/:teamId/invitations trusts the URL team_id as authorization. WORKED THE PROBLEM: the invitation table existed (M2 Task 1) but the invitation ENDPOINTS did not -- this was the natural place the AI would reproduce the IDOR (auth-only, no ownership check, exactly the module's 'training data has auth middleware but not per-resource ownership' pattern). I delegated building POST /teams/{team_id}/invitations (create), POST /.../{token}/accept, GET /.../invitations, DELETE /.../invitations/{id} with the ownership guard EXPLICITLY required: require_owner_or_admin(db, team_id, user.id) BEFORE any DB insert on create (team_router.py:133) and on list (team_router.py:162); require_owner on revoke (team_router.py:186). LIVE VERIFICATION (m4_idor_probe.py, 9 cases): Bob (authenticated, non-member) create invitation -> 403 'team admin required'; Bob list -> 403; Bob revoke -> 403 'team owner required'; owner create -> 201 pending; duplicate pending -> 409; owner revoke -> 204; accept after revoke -> 400; accept first -> 200 member created; accept SECOND TIME (replay) -> 400 'invitation not found, expired, or already used' -- one-time use confirmed via single transaction (status flip + member insert + used_at commit atomically, IntegrityError rolls back all). The IDOR is closed: URL team_id is NEVER treated as authorization; ownership is verified against teams.created_by or team_members.role='admin' before any mutation. Edge I chose to document rather than change: the accept endpoint intentionally allows ANY authenticated user with the token to accept (token = bearer of acceptance intent); scenario constraint 'prevents unauthorized acceptance and replay abuse' is satisfied via one-time token + atomic transaction + expiry/status checks. The lesson lands: the IDOR is the #1 AI security failure because ownership verification is business logic, not a pattern -- the guard must be in the PROMPT as a hard constraint, and proven live, not assumed.
evidence: team_router.py:133 require_owner_or_admin before create; :162 on list; :186 require_owner on revoke
